newsitem.title: INDIA: India's SEBI allows foreign investment in gilts.
newsitem.headline: India's SEBI allows foreign investment in gilts.

text.p: India's markets regulator, the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), on Thursday said it had permitted foreign institutions to invest in dated government securities.
"It was decided to permit FIIs (foreign institutional investors) to invest in dated government securities," the market watchdog said in a statement.
SEBI said it would allow FII-owned proprietary funds that were regulated by their home regulators or were registered with their tax authorities.
"It was also decided that the requirements for FIIs...to be broad-based would be removed," it added.
"This would facilitate investment by pilot funds or seed funds which aim to estabilish a track record prior to wide distribution of these funds," the statement added.
